executiveSummary: Analysis of 21 surveillance reports spanning October 2025 through May 2026 from ECDC and PAHO reveals multiple concurrent biological threats across the Americas and Europe. The most pressing concerns include ongoing Avian Influenza A(H5N1) activity in the Americas with zoonotic spillover risk, a resurgent dengue season, and the start of the Southern Hemisphere influenza season coinciding with RSV co-circulation. Mpox continues to spread in the Americas region, while pertussis resurges across multiple countries indicating potential vaccine coverage gaps. Yellow fever activity and measles importation risks add to an unusually complex multi-threat landscape requiring coordinated regional response.
bottomLine: The Americas face a high-complexity, multi-pathogen threat environment in 2025-2026, anchored by H5N1 zoonotic risk, dengue surge, and simultaneous respiratory virus co-circulation demanding immediate cross-sectoral surveillance reinforcement.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Multiple PAHO epidemiological updates issued November 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained regional activity
Zoonotic spillover risk to humans from ongoing animal reservoir activity across the Americas
threats.action: Enhance human-animal interface surveillance, enforce PPE protocols for exposed workers, activate pandemic preparedness protocols at national health ministries

threats.name: Dengue
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued February 2026 suggesting elevated case burden
Historical pattern of early-year peaks in Latin America consistent with ongoing transmission
threats.action: Strengthen vector control programs, activate early warning systems, ensure hospital surge capacity in endemic countries

threats.name: Seasonal Influenza / Respiratory Virus Co-circulation
threats.pathogen: Influenza A/B viruses, Respiratory Syncytial Virus
signals: PAHO alert 27 April 2026 marking start of Southern Hemisphere influenza season
Prior January 2026 alert flagging simultaneous influenza and RSV circulation creating dual-strain healthcare burden
threats.action: Accelerate Southern Hemisphere influenza vaccination campaigns, prepare ICU surge plans, monitor healthcare worker infection rates

threats.name: Mpox
signals: PAHO epidemiological update 23 April 2026 confirming ongoing transmission in the Americas
Sustained need for repeated updates indicates failure to achieve containment
threats.action: Expand vaccination coverage among high-risk populations, strengthen contact tracing and case isolation, coordinate cross-border reporting

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two separate PAHO alerts issued December 2025 and March 2026 indicating persistent and resurging transmission
Dual-season alert pattern suggests waning immunity and potential vaccine coverage gaps across age groups
threats.action: Audit vaccination coverage rates, implement catch-up immunization campaigns, prioritize booster doses for healthcare workers and pregnant women

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued 13 March 2026 signaling active risk in the region
Potential sylvatic cycle amplification coinciding with peak vector season
threats.action: Ensure vaccination coverage in endemic and at-risk zones, enhance entomological surveillance, issue travel health advisories

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO alert 3 February 2026 highlighting importation and outbreak risk in the region
Alert implies sub-optimal herd immunity thresholds in multiple countries
threats.action: Conduct vaccination coverage audits, activate outbreak response protocols, strengthen port-of-entry surveillance

threats.name: Chikungunya
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued 10 February 2026 indicating active transmission risk
Co-circulation with dengue virus complicates clinical differentiation and case management
threats.action: Enhance Aedes vector surveillance, improve clinical diagnostic capacity to differentiate from dengue, alert border health authorities

diseases: Communicable disease threats (ECDC weekly reports - multiple pathogens)

amrSignals: No explicit AMR-specific alerts identified in the 21 reports; however, Bordetella pertussis resurging despite vaccination programs warrants investigation into potential immune escape variants
Sustained dengue and chikungunya co-circulation increases risk of broad-spectrum antibiotic misuse for undifferentiated febrile illness, potentially driving community AMR pressure in the Americas
emergingPatterns: Simultaneous multi-pathogen respiratory threat (Influenza + RSV) in January 2026 followed by new Southern Hemisphere influenza season onset by April 2026 suggests compressed inter-season intervals
Dual pertussis alerts within three months (December 2025 and March 2026) indicate accelerating resurgence inconsistent with background noise, potentially reflecting population-level waning immunity
Concurrent arboviral threats (Dengue, Chikungunya, Yellow Fever) in the Americas during early 2026 suggest Aedes vector pressure at historically high levels
H5N1 requiring two separate PAHO regional updates within four months indicates failure to suppress animal reservoir activity and elevated pandemic preparedness concern
PAHO alert on GLP-1 receptor agonist misuse is a novel pharmacovigilance signal suggesting counterfeit or diverted medications entering circulation with potential for indirect public health harms
